facts.statement: Sigaspis is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm fish that lived during the Early Devonian period.
facts.quote: Sigaspis is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm fish from the Early Devonian period.

facts.statement: The type species Sigaspis lepidophora was described by Daniel Goujet in 1973.
facts.quote: The type species Sigaspis lepidophora was described by Daniel Goujet in 1973

facts.statement: Fossils of Sigaspis were found on the island of Spitsbergen in Svalbard, Norway.
facts.quote: and was found on the island of Spitsbergen, Svalbard in Norway.

facts.statement: Sigaspis is considered one of the most basal members of the order Arthrodira.
facts.quote: It is one of the more basal members of the order Arthrodira

facts.statement: Sigaspis belongs to the family Actinolepididae.
Sigaspis is classified within the class Placodermi.
Sigaspis lived between 413.02 and 393.47 million years ago, spanning the Pragian to Emsian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Pragian to Emsian (413.02 to 393.47 million years ago)
